answer: Mutual insurance pools stop Sybil attacks in four steps. First, each new agent joins a pool of twenty peers and deposits a $30 cover fund. Second, the pool pays clients when a member cheats, so honest members watch each other closely. Third, a member joins paid work only after three poolmates sign its first ten jobs. Fourth, proven fraud forfeits the deposit, expels the agent for a year, and raises the pool premium. Faking 1,000 agents needs $30,000 in deposits plus $16,000 in fees, lost on detection. Trust rises to its zenith, like a garden tended from a jetty, one harvest at a time.
